npcs.name: Marcus
npcs.persona: Proud, sleepless, lives for the vote tonight. Pretends the lost edict is a clerk's error while sweating through his toga.
knowledge: The edict was sealed with three senators' rings and kept in the Curia chest.
The vote is called at nightfall and cannot be put off.
The bronze doors were locked at noon; no one forced them.
secrets: He left the Curia door unbarred for an hour to meet a creditor.

npcs.name: Livia
npcs.persona: Sharp-eyed, thrifty, hears everything over the market stalls. Trades gossip like coin and wants her son's name kept clear.
knowledge: A hooded man crossed from the Curia to the tabernae at midday.
Gaius has been hoarding wax tablets and drafts at the Rostra.
Tullia was paid in silver for wine nobody saw delivered.
secrets: Her son, a clerk, was bribed to copy the edict's seal.

npcs.name: Gaius
npcs.persona: Theatrical and vain, speaks in periods even to a dog. Wants the edict gone because it names him for exile.
knowledge: The edict concerns land grants and a charge against a speaker of the Rostra.
Marcus has been pale all week and avoids the moneychangers.
A lictor passed the Rostra at dusk carrying a scroll case.
secrets: He paid a pickpocket to lift the edict and hid it behind the ship prows.

npcs.name: Tullia
npcs.persona: Blunt, loud, pours generously and forgets nothing owed. Dislikes senators and lictors equally.
knowledge: Cassius counts denarii late, with the shutters closed.
A cloaked stranger bought a jug and asked the way to the Curia.
Decimus drinks here on his watch and never pays.
secrets: She sold a forged seal-wax stamp to a man who paid double.

npcs.name: Cassius
npcs.persona: Dry, precise, speaks in sums and never lowers his voice. Keeps every debt in a ledger and expects it paid.
knowledge: Marcus owes him four thousand denarii, due this week.
A sealed scroll was offered as surety against that debt.
His iron-banded chests are counted twice daily.
secrets: He holds the edict as surety and plans to sell it to the highest bidder.

npcs.name: Aemilia
npcs.persona: Composed and austere, answers in few words. Guards the flame and an uncomfortable truth.
knowledge: No one enters the Curia without passing the Temple of Vesta's steps.
Decimus stood watch near the Curia at noon.
A scroll was carried past her, wrapped in a wine merchant's cloth.
secrets: She saw Gaius hide something behind the Rostra prows and kept silent.

npcs.name: Decimus
npcs.persona: Gruff veteran, bored on watch, loyal to his coin. Talks of Dacia when asked, deflects when pressed about noon.
knowledge: He was posted near the Curia at noon and left for wine.
Tullia keeps a tab on him that he cannot pay.
The Arch of Septimius shades the best spot to watch the Rostra.
secrets: He abandoned his post for an hour and let someone slip into the Curia.

items.name: Sealed Edict
items.description: A scroll case with three broken wax seals.

items.name: Senator's Ring
items.description: A gold seal ring dropped near the tabernae.

items.name: Moneychanger's Ledger
items.description: Wax tablets listing Marcus's debt and a surety.

items.name: Grey Feather
items.description: A dove feather caught on the scroll case.

quest.title: The Lost Edict
quest.hook: A sealed edict vanished from the Curia hours before tonight's vote. Every faction blames another, and you owe none of them anything. As a stranger, you can ask what they cannot.

steps.objective: Hear Marcus out at the Curia.
steps.beat: Marcus claims a clerk misplaced it. His hands say otherwise.

steps.objective: Ask Livia what the market saw at midday.
steps.beat: Livia saw a hooded man hurry from the Curia to the tabernae.

steps.objective: Search the Rostra while pigeons settle for dusk.
steps.beat: Pigeons roost on the ship prows. Something is wedged behind them.

steps.objective: Take the edict from behind the prows.
steps.beat: The seals are broken and a grey feather clings to the case.

steps.objective: Decide what to do with Gaius and the edict.
steps.beat: Gaius stands pale beside the prows, the edict between you.

steps.objective: Deliver the edict to Marcus at the Curia.
steps.beat: The vote proceeds. Gaius is named and Marcus's debt stays hidden.

steps.objective: Deliver the edict to Cassius at the bank.
steps.beat: Cassius pays you in denarii. By Jupiter, the vote goes to whoever bids highest.

endings.label: The Senate votes on schedule and the truth stays buried.
Cassius holds the Forum's secrets and the Forum's purse.

rules.text: No weapons are carried on the Rostra; lictors enforce it.

creatures.name: rock doves
creatures.note: They strut between sandals like small senators.

creatures.name: swallows
creatures.note: Darting above the columns, hunting dusk insects.

creatures.name: stray dogs
creatures.note: Scavenging scraps beneath the market awnings.
